title: Interim-plan downgrade safety-net: automated prorated overage credits and negative-balance guardrail
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem summary: Enterprise customers occasionally request plan downgrades mid-billing-cycle (committed capacity / reserved capacity -> lower tier or pay-as-you-go). Current behavior produces immediate metering deltas and either: 1) negative balances that block usage, or 2) unexpected invoice overages without clear, auditable credits. Finance receives ad-hoc support tickets and issues manual refunds or one-off credits, which is slow and error-prone. We need a deterministic, auditable workflow to (a) compute provisional prorated credits for the remaining cycle, (b) surface the adjustment to customers in the Console, and (c) finalize ledger entries in a way that satisfies accounting and supportability constraints.
proposal:
Design proposal: implement an automated 'Interim Downgrade Credit' flow with these behaviors: 
- Trigger: downgrade accepted (self-serve or sales-assisted) creates a downgrade-event in billing service. 
- Calculation: compute prorated delta between old-tier committed cost and new-tier effective cost for the remaining billing period, taking into account any reserved capacity refunds, committed discounts, and currency/rounding rules. 
- Prevent negative-balance blocking: if a downgrade would drive an account balance negative, create a provisional credit token that updates the Console balance UI (soft credit) and allow a configurable negative-balance safety net (e.g., -$1000) while reconciliation runs. 
- Credit issuance: create a pending invoice-adjustment line item (type: provisional-credit) visible in invoices and the audit trail. Finalize the provisional-credit as an actual credit entry after the next reconciliation window (24 hours) to guard against rapid re-downgrades/abuse. 
- Admin override: Support finance/support to manually issue refunds instead of credits with an idempotent admin API. 
- Notifications: send email and Console notification with details and links to 'How this credit was calculated'. 
- Rollout: start with Sales-assisted downgrades (enterprise only) behind a feature flag, then expand to self-serve after validation. 
Edge cases & constraints: 
- Exchange rates: use billing-day rate for currency conversions; record rate on ledger entry. 
- Rounding: always round credit down to customer (favor customer) for visible balance; keep precise cents in ledger for reconciliation with finance. 
- Usage spikes: if usage after downgrade causes immediate overage, overage billing is computed against the new tier; the provisional credit can be applied to the invoice balancing the net owed. 
- Accounting compliance: all provisional to final transitions must be auditable with immutable ledger IDs; requires Finance sign-off and GAAP alignment.
acceptance_criteria:
- Downgrade event creates a provisional-credit line item in billing service and visible in Console within 60s.
- Provisional credits convert to finalized ledger credit after reconciliation window (configurable, default 24h).
- Customers see updated balance and an explanatory note in invoice UI.
- Negative-balance safety net prevents immediate account suspension for downgrades up to configured threshold.
- Finance team can query and export a reconciliation report for all provisional -> final transitions.
- Automated end-to-end test covering reserve refunds + currency conversion + rounding rules in CI.
- Security review completed for admin override endpoints.
implementation_notes:
- Backend: billing service (billing-ledger) needs new 'provisional_credit' record type + reconciliation worker.
- Console: invoice UI changes and a new 'credit details' modal (content from Confluence doc).
- API: public admin API for manual refunds + idempotency keys.
- Observability: add Grafana panels for provisional-credit count, reconciliation failures, and median time-to-finalize.
- Metrics: track MTTF (downgrade -> finalized), volume of provisional credits, manual refund rate.
- Finance: create exportable CSV schema and day-of-exchange-rate field.
- Security: require SSO+RBAC for manual refund endpoints and audit log entries for each action.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Immediate credit vs delayed finalization: immediate refunds improve UX but increase fraud/abuse and accounting churn; delaying by 24h reduces risk but may frustrate some customers.
- Complexity: currency and committed-discount edge cases add implementation overhead and testing burden.
- GAAP/regulatory: Finance may require additional conservative holds; could delay ship.
- Support load: initial rollout may increase support tickets; mitigate with clear UI messages and link to self-serve docs.
